name: Question 13
worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as

$$
\int \frac{5}{9-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{5}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{3})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{artanh}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{3})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{3}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and compute it, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{5}{9-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{(\frac{x}{3})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{9}\int \frac{1}{1-{u}^{2}}\cdot 3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{1-{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that this result is subject to the condition $|\frac{x}{3}|<1.$

EXPLANATION

Let's rewrite our integral as ∫59−x2dx=59∫11−(x3)2dx.

This integral resembles the basic integral for the inverse hyperbolic tangent, ∫11−u2du=artanh⁡u+C.

The only difference is that instead of u2 as the variable, we have (x3)2.

So, let's substitute u=x3. Differentiating, we get dudx=13⟹dx=3du.

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of u and compute it, as follows: ∫59−x2dx=59∫11−(x3)2dx=59∫11−u2⋅3du=53∫du1−u2=53artanh⁡u+C=53artanh⁡(x3)+C

Note that this result is subject to the condition |x3|<1.
